Claude responded: Problem it solves: Lets you get chat content out of AI web UIs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Meta AI, and others) as a proper file instead of…

Fetched: GitHub - Covai-Labs/ai-chat-exporter: A simple, privacy-focused browser extension to export AI chats from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Qwen, Perplexity, DeepSeek, and Meta AI to Markdown or JSON.https://github.com/Covai-Labs/ai-chat-exporter
Fetched: GitHub - Covai-Labs/ai-chat-exporter: A simple, privacy-focused browser extension to export AI chats from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Qwen, Perplexity, DeepSeek, and Meta AI to Markdown or JSON.

Problem it solves: Lets you get chat content out of AI web UIs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Meta AI, and others) as a proper file instead of copy-pasting manually. All conversion happens locally in the browser, nothing sent to a server.

Who it's for: People who want to archive, share, or move AI conversations — e.g. into Obsidian/note-taking, email, docs, or a different AI platform to continue a conversation elsewhere.

Strongest features:

  • Genuinely local/privacy-first — no telemetry, no external calls.
  • Broad platform coverage (14+ AI chat sites).
  • Multiple export formats: Markdown, JSON (schema'd), HTML, PDF, .doc, PNG.
  • "Chat continuation" — push your current conversation into another platform or straight into Obsidian via URI.
  • Rich-text clipboard copy for pasting into docs/emails.
  • Side-panel support on Chromium.

Main limitations:

  • README explicitly says it was built for personal use, isn't very polished, and formatting may break when a chat platform's UI changes (fragile, since it likely relies on DOM scraping).
  • Small project: 17 stars, 4 forks, 1 watcher — thin community, so bug fixes may lag.
  • Author tests mainly on Firefox; Chromium support is "minimally tested."
  • Chrome Web Store version can lag behind GitHub/Firefox releases.
  • MPL-2.0 licensed but small single-maintainer feel — bus-factor risk.

Recommendation: Worth trying if you want a no-frills, privacy-respecting way to export chats, especially into Obsidian, since that's exactly your workflow. Given it's DOM-scraping based, expect occasional breakage when platforms update their UI, and don't rely on it for anything mission-critical. Since you're on Fedora, Firefox add-on is the safer install path over the Chromium build.

Thought for 19s

A few structural issues are holding it back from converting readers into stargazers — here's what would move the needle most:

Embed real screenshots, not just a video thumbnailRight now the only visual is a YouTube thumbnail link. Add 2-3 actual PNG screenshots inline (export popup, live preview, PNG output) right under the title — most people decide to star within seconds of landing, before clicking an external video.
Add a visible star askRepos that explicitly ask ("If this saved you time, please ⭐ the repo") measurably convert more browsers into stars. Put one line near the top or bottom, not just implied by store badges.
Add a star-history chartEmbed a star-history.com badge/image near the bottom. It's a small addition that signals momentum and social proof, which itself drives more stars.
Add a permissions/trust sectionYou claim privacy-first but never list the manifest permissions or explain why each is needed (host access, clipboard, downloads). Browser-extension users are wary; a short 'What this extension can access, and why' table builds the trust your pitch relies on.
Add a short FAQ/Troubleshooting sectionThe README already flags that DOM changes break exporters. A 'my export looks wrong / platform X isn't working' FAQ reduces duplicate issues and shows the project is maintained, which matters to anyone evaluating whether to rely on it.
Add CI and download-count badgesYou have GitHub Actions workflows but no CI/build-passing badge. Also pull real install counts from the Chrome/Firefox stores if available — numbers next to the version badges add credibility at a glance.
Add a table of contentsThe header already links to anchors (Quick Install, Features, etc.) inconsistently. A proper clickable TOC near the top makes a long README scannable, which matters since yours has grown substantially since the last version.
Differentiate from alternativesThere are several AI-chat exporters on the store. A short 'Why this one' comparison (local-only, cross-model continuation, PKM integration) gives a skimming visitor a concrete reason to pick and star yours over a competitor.

Beyond the README itself: stars mostly come from distribution, not polish — post on r/ObsidianMD and r/firefox, submit to Awesome-lists (awesome-chatgpt, awesome-browser-extensions), and reply on relevant Show HN/Reddit threads where people ask "how do I export ChatGPT chats". A great README converts visitors who already arrived; it doesn't bring them.
